f: Sawm
b: Fasting: refraining from food, drink and marital relations from dawn until sunset for Allah's sake. The Quran says to eat and drink until dawn, then complete the fast until night.
arabic: صَوْم

f: Suhoor
b: The pre-dawn meal eaten before a day of fasting. The Prophet ﷺ said: Take suhoor, for in suhoor there is blessing.
arabic: سُحُور

f: Iftar
b: Breaking the fast at sunset, and the meal eaten then. The Prophet ﷺ said that when night comes, day departs and the sun has set, the fasting person breaks the fast.
arabic: إِفْطَار

f: Niyyah
b: Intention: the aim in the heart behind an action. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever goes to bed intending to pray at night but is overcome by sleep until morning has what he intended recorded for him.
arabic: نِيَّة

f: Taqwa
b: Mindfulness of Allah that guards a person from what displeases Him. Allah prescribed fasting for us, as for those before us, so that we may attain taqwa.
arabic: تَقْوَى

f: Tarawih
b: The night prayer of Ramadan; the name means 'rests', from the pauses between sets of rak'ahs. The Prophet ﷺ led it in the mosque for a few nights, then stopped, fearing it would be made obligatory.
arabic: تَرَاوِيح

f: Qiyam al-Layl
b: Standing in prayer at night: spending part of the night in voluntary prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said the best prayer after the obligatory prayers is prayer at night.
arabic: قِيَامُ اللَّيْلِ

f: Tahajjud
b: Voluntary prayer at night; the word carries the sense of giving up sleep to pray. Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to pray part of the night with the Quran as extra worship for him.
arabic: تَهَجُّد

f: Witr
b: Literally 'odd'. The odd-numbered prayer that ends the night's prayers; the Prophet ﷺ said it makes what one has prayed at night odd.
arabic: وِتْر

f: I'tikaf
b: Staying in the mosque for a time, devoted to worship. The Quran mentions believers who are 'staying for worship in the mosques'.
arabic: اِعْتِكَاف

f: Laylat al-Qadr
b: The Night of Decree (or Power), a night in Ramadan in which the Quran was sent down. Allah says: Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree.
arabic: لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ

f: Zakat al-Fitr
b: The charity of breaking the fast, given at the end of Ramadan. The Prophet ﷺ made it due for every Muslim, young or old, and ordered it paid before the Eid prayer.
arabic: زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرِ

f: Sadaqah
b: Charity given for Allah's sake, especially voluntary giving. The Prophet ﷺ said: every act of kindness is sadaqah.
arabic: صَدَقَة

f: Fidyah
b: Literally 'ransom': feeding a needy person in place of fasts one cannot keep or make up later. Ibn Abbas said it is for the elderly unable to fast, who feed one needy person for each day.
arabic: فِدْيَة

f: Qada
b: Making up a missed act of worship later, such as missed Ramadan fasts. Aishah (RA) said women were ordered to make up fasts missed during menstruation, but not prayers.
arabic: قَضَاء

f: Tajweed
b: Reciting the Quran correctly, giving each letter its due sound and following the rules of recitation. Allah says: recite the Quran with measured recitation.
arabic: تَجْوِيد

f: Khatm
b: Completing a full reading of the Quran from beginning to end. The Prophet ﷺ advised Abdullah ibn Amr to complete it once a month.
arabic: خَتْم

f: Surah
b: A chapter of the Quran; there are 114 surahs. Allah challenges anyone in doubt about the Quran to produce a single surah like it.
arabic: سُورَة

f: Ayah
b: A verse of the Quran. The word also means 'sign': Allah says that in the creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day there are signs for people of understanding.
arabic: آيَة

f: Dua
b: Supplication: calling upon Allah and asking Him directly. Allah says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you.
arabic: دُعَاء

f: Dhikr
b: Remembrance of Allah, in the heart and on the tongue. Allah says: Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
arabic: ذِكْر

f: Istighfar
b: Asking Allah for forgiveness, as in saying Astaghfirullah. Prophet Nuh told his people: Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed, He is ever a Perpetual Forgiver.
arabic: اِسْتِغْفَار

f: Tawbah
b: Repentance: turning back to Allah after a sin. Allah says: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance.
arabic: تَوْبَة

f: Muhasabah
b: Self-accounting: honestly reviewing one's own deeds. Allah says: let every soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow.
arabic: مُحَاسَبَة

f: Sha'ban
b: The month just before Ramadan. The Prophet ﷺ fasted more in Sha'ban than in any other month apart from Ramadan.
arabic: شَعْبَان

f: Eid al-Fitr
b: The festival of breaking the fast that marks the end of Ramadan. The Prophet ﷺ would not go out on its morning until he had eaten some dates.
arabic: عِيدُ الْفِطْرِ

f: Takbir
b: Saying Allahu Akbar, 'Allah is the Greatest'. In the fasting verses, Allah says He wants us to complete the count of days and proclaim His greatness for guiding us.
arabic: تَكْبِير

f: Sunnah
b: The way of the Prophet ﷺ: his teachings and practice; also used for recommended acts. To men set on nonstop prayer and fasting, he said: I fast and break my fast, I pray and sleep... whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.
arabic: سُنَّة

f: Fard
b: An obligatory duty. A man asked what Allah had made obligatory for him in prayer and fasting; the Prophet ﷺ named the five daily prayers and the fast of Ramadan, saying anything more is voluntary.
arabic: فَرْض

f: Rak'ah
b: One unit of the prayer, made up of standing, bowing and prostrating. The Prophet ﷺ said: when you enter the mosque, pray two rak'ahs before sitting.
arabic: رَكْعَة

f: When breaking your fast at iftar
b: The thirst is gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if Allah wills.
arabic: ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ وَابْتَلَّتِ الْعُرُوقُ وَثَبَتَ الأَجْرُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
translit: Dhahabaz-zama'u wabtallatil-'uruqu wa thabatal-ajru in sha' Allah

f: If you come upon Laylatul Qadr - taught by the Prophet ﷺ to Aishah
b: O Allah, You are Pardoning and You love to pardon, so pardon me.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي

f: By day or by night, with firm faith: Sayyid al-Istighfar, the best way to seek forgiveness
b: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, keeping Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
arabic: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَىَّ وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ
translit: Allahumma anta Rabbi, la ilaha illa anta, khalaqtani wa ana 'abduka, wa ana 'ala 'ahdika wa wa'dika mastata'tu, a'udhu bika min sharri ma sana'tu, abu'u laka bini'matika 'alayya, wa abu'u laka bidhanbi, faghfir li, fa innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa anta

f: After eating at someone's home: the dua the Prophet ﷺ made for his host
b: May fasting people break their fast with you, may the righteous eat your food, and may the angels send blessings upon you.
arabic: أَفْطَرَ عِنْدَكُمُ الصَّائِمُونَ وَأَكَلَ طَعَامَكُمُ الأَبْرَارُ وَصَلَّتْ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ
translit: Aftara 'indakumus-sa'imun, wa akala ta'amakumul-abrar, wa sallat 'alaykumul-mala'ikah

f: Any time: the dua the Prophet ﷺ made most often (Bukhari 6389)
b: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
arabic: رَبَّنَآ ءَاتِنَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ
translit: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanatan wa fil-akhirati hasanatan wa qina 'adhaban-nar

f: Asking Allah to keep your heart firm on guidance
b: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
arabic: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْوَهَّابُ
translit: Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana wa hab lana mil-ladunka rahmah, innaka antal-Wahhab

f: For your parents: Allah tells us in the Quran to say this
b: My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up when I was small.
arabic: رَّبِّ ٱرْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا

f: When seeking knowledge: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to say this
b: My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
arabic: رَّبِّ زِدْنِى عِلْمًا

f: Asking Allah to accept a good deed: said by Ibrahim and Ismail while building the Ka'bah
b: Our Lord, accept this from us. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
arabic: رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ

f: In distress: the call of Yunus in the darkness, which Allah answered (Quran 21:88)
b: There is no god except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.
arabic: لَّآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَـٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ
translit: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu minaz-zalimin

f: For your spouse and children: a dua of the servants of the Most Merciful
b: Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and children comfort to our eyes, and make us an example for the righteous.
arabic: رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَٰجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّـٰتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَٱجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
translit: Rabbana hab lana min azwajina wa dhurriyyatina qurrata a'yunin waj'alna lil-muttaqina imama

f: For yourself and your children to keep up prayer: a dua of Ibrahim
b: My Lord, make me one who establishes prayer, and from my descendants too. Our Lord, accept my supplication.
arabic: رَبِّ ٱجْعَلْنِى مُقِيمَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى ۚ رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَآءِ
translit: Rabbij'alni muqimas-salati wa min dhurriyyati, Rabbana wa taqabbal du'a'

f: Quran 2:183 - Fasting is prescribed, and its purpose
b: O you who believe, fasting has been decreed for you as it was decreed for those before you, so that you may become righteous (attain taqwa).
arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
translit: Ya ayyuhal-ladhina amanu kutiba 'alaykumus-siyamu kama kutiba 'alal-ladhina min qablikum la'allakum tattaqun

f: Quran 2:184 - A limited number of days, and those excused
b: Fasting is for a limited number of days; whoever is ill or travelling makes up an equal number of other days. For those who can fast only with extreme difficulty, there is a ransom (fidyah): feeding a poor person. Doing more good is better, and fasting is best for you, if you only knew.
arabic: أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَٰتٍ ۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ ۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّهُۥ ۚ وَأَن تَصُومُوا۟ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
translit: Ayyaman ma'dudat, faman kana minkum maridan aw 'ala safarin fa'iddatun min ayyamin ukhar, wa 'alal-ladhina yutiqunahu fidyatun ta'amu miskin, faman tatawwa'a khayran fahuwa khayrun lah, wa an tasumu khayrun lakum in kuntum ta'lamun

f: Quran 2:185 - The month of the Quran, and Allah wants ease for you
b: In the month of Ramadan the Quran was revealed, a guidance for people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. Whoever witnesses the month is to fast it; whoever is ill or travelling makes up an equal number of other days. Allah wants ease for you, not hardship, and wants you to complete the number of days and glorify Him for guiding you, that you may be grateful.
arabic: شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَـٰتٍ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ ۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ ۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۗ يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُوا۟ ٱلْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَىٰكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
translit: Shahru Ramadanal-ladhi unzila fihil-Qur'anu hudan lin-nasi wa bayyinatin minal-huda wal-furqan, faman shahida minkumush-shahra falyasumh, wa man kana maridan aw 'ala safarin fa'iddatun min ayyamin ukhar, yuridullahu bikumul-yusra wa la yuridu bikumul-'usra wa litukmilul-'iddata wa litukabbirullaha 'ala ma hadakum wa la'allakum tashkurun

f: Quran 2:186 - When My servants ask you about Me
b: When Allah's servants ask about Him, He is near. He answers the call of the caller when he calls upon Him, so let them respond to Him and believe in Him, that they may be rightly guided.
arabic: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ
translit: Wa idha sa'alaka 'ibadi 'anni fa inni qarib, ujibu da'watad-da'i idha da'an, falyastajibu li walyu'minu bi la'allahum yarshudun

f: Quran 2:187 - The nights of the fast, and eating until dawn (Arabic: excerpt)
b: On the nights of the fast, spouses are permitted to each other (not during i'tikaf in the mosques); they are a garment for one another. Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn is distinct from the black, then complete the fast until night (sunset). These are Allah's limits.
arabic: وَكُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ ٱلْخَيْطُ ٱلْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ ٱلْخَيْطِ ٱلْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ ۖ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا۟ ٱلصِّيَامَ إِلَى ٱلَّيْلِ
translit: Wa kulu washrabu hatta yatabayyana lakumul-khaytul-abyadu minal-khaytil-aswadi minal-fajr, thumma atimmus-siyama ilal-layl

f: Quran 97:1-5 - Surah al-Qadr: the Night of Decree
b: Allah sent the Quran down on the Night of Decree, a night better than a thousand months. In it the angels and the Spirit (Jibreel) descend by their Lord's permission for every matter. It is peace until the emergence of dawn.
arabic: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ سَلَـٰمٌ هِىَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ
translit: Inna anzalnahu fi laylatil-qadr. Wa ma adraka ma laylatul-qadr. Laylatul-qadri khayrun min alfi shahr. Tanazzalul-mala'ikatu war-ruhu fiha bi'idhni rabbihim min kulli amr. Salamun hiya hatta matla'il-fajr.

f: Quran 44:3 - The Book sent down on a blessed night
b: Allah says: We sent it (the clear Book) down during a blessed night; indeed, We were to warn mankind.
arabic: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَـٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَـٰرَكَةٍ ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ
translit: Inna anzalnahu fi laylatin mubarakah, inna kunna mundhirin

f: Quran 2:255 - Ayat al-Kursi: who Allah is
b: No god but Allah, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining; no drowsiness or sleep overtakes Him. All in the heavens and earth is His; none intercedes except by His permission. He knows what is before and after them, and they grasp of His knowledge only what He wills. His Kursi extends over heavens and earth, guarding them tires Him not; He is the Most High, the Most Great.
arabic: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِۦ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ
translit: Allahu la ilaha illa huwal-Hayyul-Qayyum, la ta'khudhuhu sinatun wa la nawm, lahu ma fis-samawati wa ma fil-ard, man dhal-ladhi yashfa'u 'indahu illa bi'idhnih, ya'lamu ma bayna aydihim wa ma khalfahum, wa la yuhituna bishay'in min 'ilmihi illa bima sha', wasi'a kursiyyuhus-samawati wal-ard, wa la ya'uduhu hifzuhuma, wa huwal-'Aliyyul-'Azim

f: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell us to eat suhoor?
b: He said: Take suhoor, for in suhoor there is blessing (Bukhari 1923).
arabic: تَسَحَّرُوا فَإِنَّ فِي السَّحُورِ بَرَكَةً

f: Zayd ibn Thabit ate suhoor with the Prophet ﷺ. How long was it between their suhoor and the adhan?
b: About the time it takes to recite fifty ayat (Bukhari 1921).
arabic: قَدْرُ خَمْسِينَ آيَةً

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about hastening to break the fast?
b: People will remain upon goodness as long as they hasten to break the fast (Bukhari 1957).
arabic: لاَ يَزَالُ النَّاسُ بِخَيْرٍ مَا عَجَّلُوا الْفِطْرَ

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ break his fast with?
b: Fresh dates, before praying. If there were none, dried dates, and if there were none, a few sips of water (Abu Dawud 2356).
arabic: يُفْطِرُ عَلَى رُطَبَاتٍ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ رُطَبَاتٌ فَعَلَى تَمَرَاتٍ فَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ حَسَا حَسَوَاتٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ
translit: Yuftiru 'ala rutabatin qabla an yusalli, fa-in lam takun rutabatun fa-'ala tamaratin, fa-in lam takun hasa hasawatin min ma'

f: What words did the Prophet ﷺ teach a fasting person to say if someone fights or insults them, and how many times?
b: 'Inni sa'im', meaning 'I am fasting', said twice (Bukhari 1894).
arabic: إِنِّي صَائِمٌ

f: Ibn Abbas compared the Prophet's ﷺ generosity in Ramadan to what?
b: The free-blowing wind. When Jibreel met him in Ramadan, he was more generous in doing good than the wind sent forth (Bukhari 6).
arabic: أَجْوَدُ بِالْخَيْرِ مِنَ الرِّيحِ الْمُرْسَلَةِ

f: Until when did the Prophet ﷺ keep up i'tikaf in the last ten days of Ramadan?
b: Until Allah took his soul. After him, his wives observed i'tikaf too (Bukhari 2026).
arabic: كَانَ يَعْتَكِفُ الْعَشْرَ الأَوَاخِرَ مِنْ رَمَضَانَ حَتَّى تَوَفَّاهُ اللَّهُ، ثُمَّ اعْتَكَفَ أَزْوَاجُهُ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ
translit: Kana ya'takiful-'ashral-awakhira min Ramadana hatta tawaffahullah, thumma'takafa azwajuhu min ba'dih

f: When the last ten nights of Ramadan began, whom did the Prophet ﷺ wake up for worship?
b: His family. Aishah said he would spend the night in worship and wake his family (Bukhari 2024).
arabic: وَأَحْيَا لَيْلَهُ، وَأَيْقَظَ أَهْلَهُ
translit: Wa ahya laylahu, wa ayqaza ahlah

f: How does this hadith end: 'Whoever gives a fasting person something to break the fast with...'?
b: '...will have a reward like his, without the fasting person's reward being reduced at all' (Tirmidhi 807).
arabic: مَنْ فَطَّرَ صَائِمًا كَانَ لَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِهِ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ لاَ يَنْقُصُ مِنْ أَجْرِ الصَّائِمِ شَيْئًا
translit: Man fattara sa'iman kana lahu mithlu ajrihi, ghayra annahu la yanqusu min ajris-sa'imi shay'a

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about praying the Ramadan night prayer with the imam until he finishes?
b: Standing in prayer for a whole night is recorded for that person. He said this in Ramadan when the Companions asked him to lead them in prayer for the rest of the night (Tirmidhi 806).
arabic: مَنْ قَامَ مَعَ الإِمَامِ حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ كُتِبَ لَهُ قِيَامُ لَيْلَةٍ
translit: Man qama ma'al-imami hatta yansarifa kutiba lahu qiyamu laylah

f: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid al-wisal, joining one day's fast to the next without eating at night?
b: Out of mercy for his Companions. When they said, 'But you do it', he said: I am not like you; my Lord gives me food and drink (Bukhari 1964).
arabic: إِنِّي لَسْتُ كَهَيْئَتِكُمْ، إِنِّي يُطْعِمُنِي رَبِّي وَيَسْقِينِ
translit: Inni lastu ka-hay'atikum, inni yut'imuni Rabbi wa yasqin

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say is the difference between our fasting and the fasting of the People of the Book?
b: Eating suhoor, the meal before dawn (Muslim 1096).
arabic: فَصْلُ مَا بَيْنَ صِيَامِنَا وَصِيَامِ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ أَكْلَةُ السَّحَرِ
translit: Faslu ma bayna siyamina wa siyami ahlil-kitabi aklatus-sahar

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about a fasting person who forgets and eats or drinks?
b: He should complete his fast, for it was Allah who fed him and gave him drink (Bukhari 1933).
arabic: فَلْيُتِمَّ صَوْمَهُ، فَإِنَّمَا أَطْعَمَهُ اللَّهُ وَسَقَاهُ
translit: Fal-yutimma sawmahu, fa-innama at'amahullahu wa saqah

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about performing Umrah in Ramadan?
b: An Umrah in Ramadan equals a Hajj (in reward). He told this to an Ansari woman who had missed the Hajj with him (Bukhari 1782).
arabic: فَإِنَّ عُمْرَةً فِي رَمَضَانَ حَجَّةٌ

f: Bilal used to call the adhan while it was still night. Until when did the Prophet ﷺ say to keep eating and drinking?
b: Until Ibn Umm Maktum called the adhan, for he did not call it until dawn had broken (Bukhari 1918).
arabic: كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّى يُؤَذِّنَ ابْنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ
translit: Kulu washrabu hatta yu'adhdhina Ibnu Ummi Maktum

f: In Madinah the Prophet ﷺ fasted the day of Ashura and told others to fast it. What changed once fasting Ramadan was prescribed?
b: Fasting Ashura became optional: whoever wished fasted it, and whoever wished left it (Bukhari 2002).
arabic: فَمَنْ شَاءَ صَامَهُ، وَمَنْ شَاءَ تَرَكَهُ
translit: Fa-man sha'a samahu, wa man sha'a tarakah

f: After hearing the ayah about the white thread and the black thread (Quran 2:187), what did Adi ibn Hatim put under his pillow?
b: A black cord and a white cord, but he could not tell them apart at night. The Prophet ﷺ explained it means the darkness of night and the whiteness of dawn (Bukhari 1916).
arabic: إِنَّمَا ذَلِكَ سَوَادُ اللَّيْلِ وَبَيَاضُ النَّهَارِ

f: At Badr (Ramadan, 2 AH), the Prophet ﷺ faced the qiblah and pleaded with Allah, hands stretched out. What did Allah promise?
b: To reinforce the believers with a thousand angels, one after another. Umar reports that Quran 8:9 was revealed then (Muslim 1763).
arabic: أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُمْ بِأَلْفٍ مِنَ الْمَلاَئِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ

f: The Companions who fought at Badr (Ramadan, 2 AH) said their number matched which earlier band of believers?
b: The companions of Talut (Saul) who crossed the river with him: just over three hundred and ten men, and only believers crossed with him (Bukhari 3957).

f: Why did Uthman ibn Affan miss the Battle of Badr (Ramadan, 2 AH)?
b: His wife, a daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, was ill. The Prophet ﷺ told him he would have the reward of a man who was at Badr, and his share of the spoils (Bukhari 3130).
arabic: إِنَّ لَكَ أَجْرَ رَجُلٍ مِمَّنْ شَهِدَ بَدْرًا وَسَهْمَهُ
translit: Inna laka ajra rajulin mimman shahida Badran wa sahmah

f: At the Conquest of Makkah (Ramadan, 8 AH), what did the Prophet ﷺ say as he struck the idols around the Ka'bah?
b: 'Truth has come and falsehood has vanished' (Quran 17:81). There were 360 idols around the Ka'bah (Bukhari 4287).
arabic: جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ الْبَاطِلُ

f: Which surah was the Prophet ﷺ reciting on his she-camel on the day of the Conquest of Makkah?
b: Surah al-Fath (The Victory), recited with tarji', a vibrating tone, as Abdullah ibn Mughaffal saw (Bukhari 4281).
arabic: وَهْوَ يَقْرَأُ سُورَةَ الْفَتْحِ يُرَجِّعُ

f: On the day of the Conquest of Makkah, who went inside the Ka'bah with the Prophet ﷺ?
b: Usamah ibn Zayd, Bilal and Uthman ibn Talhah, one of the Ka'bah's key-keepers. The Prophet ﷺ stayed inside a long time and prayed there (Bukhari 2988).

f: The Prophet ﷺ was shown that on the morning after Laylatul Qadr he would prostrate in water and mud. How did this come true?
b: That night it rained and the mosque's palm-leaf roof leaked. In the morning Abu Sa'id saw traces of water and mud on the Prophet's ﷺ forehead (Bukhari 2027).
arabic: وَقَدْ رَأَيْتُنِي أَسْجُدُ فِي مَاءٍ وَطِينٍ مِنْ صَبِيحَتِهَا
translit: Wa qad ra'aytuni asjudu fi ma'in wa tinin min sabihatiha

f: When his wife Safiyyah visited the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque during his i'tikaf, why did he tell two passing men, 'She is Safiyyah'?
b: He feared Satan might put a bad thought in their hearts. This was in the last ten days of Ramadan (Bukhari 2035).
arabic: عَلَى رِسْلِكُمَا إِنَّمَا هِيَ صَفِيَّةُ بِنْتُ حُيَىٍّ
translit: 'Ala rislikuma, innama hiya Safiyyatu bintu Huyayy

f: How many surahs are in the Quran, and which one comes last?
b: 114 surahs. The last is Surah An-Nas (Mankind), Surah 114.

f: Which surah begins the 30th and final juz of the Quran?
b: Surah An-Naba (78). Its first word is 'Amma, which is why this juz is known as Juz 'Amma.
arabic: عَمَّ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ

f: How many ayat does Surah Al-Fatihah have?
b: Seven. Al-Fatihah means 'The Opener', and it is the first surah of the Quran.

f: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ call the greatest surah in the Quran?
b: Al-Fatihah. He said it is 'the seven oft-repeated (ayat) and the Great Quran' that was given to him.
arabic: هِيَ السَّبْعُ الْمَثَانِي وَالْقُرْآنُ الْعَظِيمُ الَّذِي أُوتِيتُهُ

f: Which is the longest surah in the Quran?
b: Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow), Surah 2, with 286 ayat.

f: Which is the shortest surah in the Quran?
b: Al-Kawthar (Surah 108), with 3 short ayat. Al-Asr and An-Nasr also have 3 ayat, but Al-Kawthar has the fewest words.

f: What did the angel first say to the Prophet ﷺ in the cave of Hira?
b: 'Read!' He ﷺ replied, 'I do not know how to read.' This happened three times, then the angel said: 'Read in the name of your Lord who created...' (Al-Alaq 96:1-3).
arabic: حَتَّى جَاءَهُ الْحَقُّ وَهُوَ فِي غَارِ حِرَاءٍ
translit: Hatta ja'ahul-haqqu wa huwa fi ghari Hira'

f: Which ayah says that the Quran was revealed in the month of Ramadan?
b: Al-Baqarah 2:185. The same ayah says: whoever of you witnesses the month, let him fast it.
arabic: شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ فِيهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ

f: According to Surah 97 of the Quran, on which night was the Quran sent down?
b: Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree): 'Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree.' Surah 97 is Surah Al-Qadr.

f: The Prophet ﷺ asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b (Abu al-Mundhir) which ayah in the Book of Allah is the greatest. Which ayah did Ubayy name?
b: Ayat al-Kursi (2:255). The Prophet ﷺ praised him: 'May knowledge be pleasant for you, Abu al-Mundhir!'
arabic: يَا أَبَا الْمُنْذِرِ أَتَدْرِي أَىُّ آيَةٍ مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ مَعَكَ أَعْظَمُ
translit: Ya Abal-Mundhir, a-tadri ayyu ayatin min Kitabillahi ma'aka a'zam

f: Who told Abu Hurayrah that if he recited Ayat al-Kursi on going to bed, a guardian from Allah would stay with him and no devil would come near him until morning?
b: Someone stealing from the Ramadan charity food, who was really a devil (shaytan). The Prophet ﷺ said: 'He told you the truth, though he is a liar.'
arabic: إِذَا أَوَيْتَ إِلَى فِرَاشِكَ فَاقْرَأْ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ
translit: Idha awayta ila firashika faqra' ayatal-kursi

f: Which two ayat did the Prophet ﷺ say will suffice whoever recites them at night?
b: The last two ayat of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:285-286).

f: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ say is equal to one third of the Quran?
b: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112): 'Say, He is Allah, the One.'
arabic: وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ إِنَّهَا لَتَعْدِلُ ثُلُثَ الْقُرْآنِ
translit: Walladhi nafsi biyadihi innaha lata'dilu thuluthal-Qur'an

f: Which surah of thirty ayat did the Prophet ﷺ say intercedes for a man until he is forgiven?
b: Surah Al-Mulk (67), which begins 'Tabarakal-ladhi biyadihil-mulk'.
arabic: إِنَّ سُورَةً مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ثَلاَثُونَ آيَةً شَفَعَتْ لِرَجُلٍ حَتَّى غُفِرَ لَهُ
translit: Inna suratan minal-Qur'ani thalathuna ayatan shafa'at li-rajulin hatta ghufira lah

f: Which is the only surah of the Quran that does not begin with 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'?
b: Surah At-Tawbah (Surah 9). It opens directly with 'Bara'atun minallahi wa rasulih'.
arabic: بَرَآءَةٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦٓ

f: Apart from Ramadan, in which month did the Prophet ﷺ fast the most?
b: Sha'ban. Aisha (RA) said she never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban.

f: Did the Prophet ﷺ fast every single day of Sha'ban?
b: Aisha (RA) said he fasted Sha'ban except a little, and she never saw him fast a whole month except Ramadan.
arabic: كَانَ يَصُومُ شَعْبَانَ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً

f: When Usama ibn Zayd noticed how much the Prophet ﷺ fasted in Sha'ban, how did the Prophet ﷺ describe that month?
b: 'A month that people neglect, between Rajab and Ramadan.'
arabic: ذَلِكَ شَهْرٌ يَغْفُلُ النَّاسُ عَنْهُ بَيْنَ رَجَبٍ وَرَمَضَانَ
translit: Dhalika shahrun yaghfulun-nasu 'anhu bayna Rajabin wa Ramadan

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say happens to our deeds in the month of Sha'ban?
b: Deeds are raised up to the Lord of the worlds, and he loved for his deeds to be raised while he was fasting.
arabic: وَهُوَ شَهْرٌ تُرْفَعُ فِيهِ الأَعْمَالُ إِلَى رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ فَأُحِبُّ أَنْ يُرْفَعَ عَمَلِي وَأَنَا صَائِمٌ
translit: Wa huwa shahrun turfa'u fihil-a'malu ila Rabbil-'alamin, fa-uhibbu an yurfa'a 'amali wa ana sa'im

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about fasting a day or two just before Ramadan?
b: None of you should fast a day or two ahead of Ramadan, unless it falls on a fast he regularly keeps.
arabic: لاَ يَتَقَدَّمَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ رَمَضَانَ بِصَوْمِ يَوْمٍ أَوْ يَوْمَيْنِ
translit: La yataqaddamanna ahadukum Ramadana bi-sawmi yawmin aw yawmayn

f: In which month did Aisha (RA) make up the Ramadan fasts she owed?
b: Sha'ban. She said she could not manage to make them up except in Sha'ban.
arabic: كَانَ يَكُونُ عَلَىَّ الصَّوْمُ مِنْ رَمَضَانَ

f: People asked the Prophet ﷺ about the crescent moons. What does the Quran say they are for?
b: Allah told him to say: 'They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj (pilgrimage).'
arabic: يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْأَهِلَّةِ

f: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Saddidu wa qaribu.' What does it mean?
b: Do good deeds properly and in moderation, and if you cannot do them perfectly, come as close as you can.
arabic: سَدِّدُوا وَقَارِبُوا

f: What did the Prophet ﷺ advise about how many good deeds to take on?
b: Take on the deeds you are able to do, for Allah does not tire (of giving reward) until you tire.
arabic: خُذُوا مِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تُطِيقُونَ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لاَ يَمَلُّ حَتَّى تَمَلُّوا
translit: Khudhu minal-'amali ma tutiqun, fa-innallaha la yamallu hatta tamallu

f: According to Quran 2:183, why was fasting prescribed for the believers?
b: So that you may become righteous (attain taqwa). It was also prescribed for those before us.
arabic: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
translit: Kutiba 'alaykumus-siyamu kama kutiba 'alal-ladhina min qablikum la'allakum tattaqun
